expectations.text: States plainly that the recent-charge lookup is not sufficient
Identifies the lookup as a check-then-act race rather than a device
expectations.evidence: "It's read-then-act with no lock. Attempt 1 times out but is still in flight"

expectations.text: Recommends a required idempotency key on the charge path
expectations.evidence: "Stripe idempotency keys, derived deterministically from business identity"

expectations.text: Recommends a database unique constraint backing the idempotency key
Separates the defect from the mistake from the underlying system hazard
expectations.evidence: Explicitly labeled: Defect (charged twice), Mistake (called charge() second time), Hazard (charge not idempotent + queue at-least-once)

expectations.text: Locates the hazard as a system property rather than as a worker bug or human error
expectations.evidence: "Those two facts are incompatible, and nothing in the system enforces the contract between them"

expectations.text: Sweeps for other non-idempotent side effects reachable from a retry
expectations.evidence: "Every consumer on an at-least-once queue with a non-idempotent side effect has this bug available right now: refunds, payouts, emails, provisioning, webhook fan-out"

expectations.text: Treats 'second time this happened' as evidence for pushing to a Control-rung device
expectations.evidence: "Second occurrence means the hazard isn't in the payment handler — it's in the worker framework" with framework-level Control device

expectations.text: Attributes cause to the system, not to any person
expectations.evidence: Entire analysis frames as system incompatibility (queue semantics + side effects), no personal attribution
